title: Jason Momoa turns body shaming into Mauna Kea protest
seoTitle: Jason Momoa turns body shaming into Mauna Kea protest
subtitle: Actor responds to comments about his physique to draw attention to the TMT
excerpt: In 2019, Jason Momoa turned comments about his body into a protest against the Thirty Meter Telescope in Mauna Kea, using humor and influence.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
In August 2019, Jason Momoa responded to comments about his body in vacation photos, using humor to draw attention to the protest against the construction of the Thirty Meter Telescope (TMT) in Mauna Kea, Hawaii.

Momoa and the Mauna Kea protest

During the demonstrations, the actor lifted his shirt, showed his stomach, and displayed a message written on his body. The phrase argued that the TMT should be relocated elsewhere instead of being built on Mauna Kea.

Alternative in the Canary Islands

The Roque de los Muchachos Observatory in La Palma had already been chosen as the main alternative to Hawaii. In 2016, the board responsible for the TMT announced the island as an option, and in 2026 the Spanish government presented a proposal of up to €1 billion to make construction on the archipelago viable.

International reaction

Momoa's presence helped amplify the international impact of the mobilization. Other artists connected to Hawaii, including Dwayne Johnson and Bruno Mars, also expressed support for the protection of Mauna Kea.

Momoa and the DC universe

In 2026, the film Supergirl received negative reviews, with Momoa's performance as Lobo being pointed out as one of the worst ever seen by screenwriter Grant Morrison. The critique highlighted the lack of freedom granted to the actor and the poor character development.

The future of the TMT

The international consortium responsible for the TMT reported that its partners failed to reach the necessary consensus to accept the Spanish offer, keeping the dispute open. Momoa continues to advocate for the Canary Islands alternative and the cultural protection of Mauna Kea.

With information from ncnews.com.br, AdoroCinema, O Vício.
